Combine coverage objects

Source: R/coverage.R
c.coverage.Rd

Combine the coverage of several runs, e.g. of tests in different directories, into a single coverage object. The counts of traces present in more than one object are added, and traces only in some of the objects are appended. Tests recorded with options(covr.record_tests = TRUE) are combined as well.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'coverage'
c(...)

Arguments

...

Coverage objects, e.g. from package_coverage() or file_coverage(). They must all be for the same package, or all have no package, like the results of file_coverage() and code_coverage(). NULL arguments are dropped.

Value

A coverage object.

Details

The result keeps the attributes of the first object, such as the package and root used for relative paths, except that the lines excluded from line coverage are the union of the excluded lines of all objects. As with package_coverage(type = c("tests", "examples")), the result only has a type if all objects have the same type.

As with any S3 method for c(), this method is only used when the first argument is a coverage object.

Examples

source_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".R")
writeLines(
  c(
    "add <- function(x, y) {",
    "  x + y",
    "}",
    "subtract <- function(x, y) {",
    "  x - y",
    "}"
  ),
  source_file
)
add_test <- tempfile(fileext = ".R")
writeLines("add(1, 2)", add_test)
subtract_test <- tempfile(fileext = ".R")
writeLines("subtract(2, 1)", subtract_test)

add_cov <- file_coverage(source_file, add_test)
subtract_cov <- file_coverage(source_file, subtract_test)
percent_coverage(add_cov)
#> [1] 50
percent_coverage(c(add_cov, subtract_cov))
#> [1] 100
